skill.name: daily.dev
skill.description: Use the daily.dev API to discover current developer articles, search topics, build feeds, manage bookmarks, and summarize community trends.
skill.summary: Find and organize current developer knowledge through daily.dev.
skill.author: dailydotdev

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, comments, and first-party URLs. Confirmed findings read API credentials from OS stores, export them into the environment, and execute a fixed network command. No prompt injection or third-party exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill retrieves plaintext tokens from operating-system credential stores without per-use confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before each credential-store read. Prefer an already-set DAILY_DEV_TOKEN or a scoped secret provider.

remediation.issue: The setup recommends exporting the token from shell startup files.
remediation.suggestion: Remove persistent shell-profile exports. Use per-session injection that limits plaintext token exposure to the required command.

remediation.issue: The endpoint list uses an executable curl and jq directive during skill rendering.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the executable directive with static documentation or a user-confirmed update command.

content.user_title: Discover Current Developer Knowledge with daily.dev
content.value_statement: Developer guidance becomes outdated when models cannot access current community discussions. This skill queries daily.dev feeds and searches to support timely, source-aware research.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve personalized, popular, discussed, and source-specific daily.dev feeds.
Search posts, publishers, tags, and technology profile entries.
Create custom feeds filtered by topics or project technologies.
Follow tags and manage profile stack entries through supported API endpoints.
Create bookmark lists and save selected articles for later review.
Summarize current articles and compare perspectives across multiple publishers.
limitations: A daily.dev Plus subscription and API token are required.
The skill can only use data and actions exposed by the public API.
Requests are limited to 60 calls per minute for each user.
GitHub analysis requires separate repository access and user approval.

use_cases.title: Track Stack Updates
use_cases.description: Build a focused feed for technologies used in active projects and review recent articles.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technology Briefings
use_cases.description: Combine popular and personalized posts into a concise weekly engineering update.

use_cases.title: Compare Technical Perspectives
use_cases.description: Search several publishers and summarize agreements, disagreements, and cited recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Articles
prompt_templates.prompt: Find five recent daily.dev posts about [topic]. Include titles, sources, dates, links, and short relevance notes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Project Feed
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this project's technologies, match them to daily.dev tags, and propose a custom feed. Ask before changing my account.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Weekly Briefing
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize my relevant daily.dev feeds for this week. Group updates by technology and highlight releases, security issues, and debates.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Multiple Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic] across daily.dev publishers. Compare evidence, identify disagreements, rank source authority, and provide a balanced conclusion with links.

output_examples.output: Five ranked articles with source names, publication dates, links, and one-sentence relevance notes.

output_examples.input: Create my weekly frontend development briefing.
output_examples.output: A grouped briefing covering notable releases, security updates, community debates, and recommended reading.

output_examples.input: Compare current opinions about server components.
output_examples.output: A balanced comparison showing shared conclusions, disputed claims, source differences, and links for further reading.

best_practices: Confirm account-changing actions before following tags, editing profiles, or creating feeds.
Use several publishers and preserve links when summarizing contested technical topics.
Respect rate-limit headers and delay retries according to the Retry-After value.
anti_patterns: Do not expose the API token in prompts, logs, source files, or third-party requests.
Do not treat community popularity as proof that technical claims are correct.
Do not scan private repositories or modify daily.dev data without clear user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require a paid daily.dev account?
faq.answer: Yes. API access requires a daily.dev Plus subscription and a personal token.

faq.question: How does the skill authenticate?
faq.answer: It sends the DAILY_DEV_TOKEN as a bearer token to the daily.dev public API.

faq.question: Can it change my daily.dev account?
faq.answer: Yes. Supported endpoints can follow tags, update stack data, create feeds, and manage bookmarks.

faq.question: Can it inspect my GitHub repositories?
faq.answer: Only when separate GitHub access is available and you approve repository analysis.

faq.question: What rate limit applies?
faq.answer: The documented limit is 60 requests per minute for each user.

faq.question: Does daily.dev guarantee article accuracy?
faq.answer: No. Community signals support discovery, but important claims should be checked against primary sources.
